children.value: > Fact From Story Specifically, it is looking at Talon Cyber Security — which has developed an enterprise browser aimed at security distributed workforces — for between $600 million and $700 million; and Dig Security — a specialist in securing data across public clouds — for between $300 million and $400 million.
> > Fact From Story Palo Alto is publicly traded and currently has a market cap of close to $70 billion. | Deduced Fact
> > > Fact From Story Both startups are less than three years old, and in both cases these would be strong outcomes compared to their existing valuations.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge Startups are often acquired by larger companies to expand their services.
> > Commonsense Knowledge A company with a market cap of $70 billion can afford to spend $1 billion to acquire startups. | Commonsense Knowledge
> Fact From Story Palo Alto is in advanced negotiations to buy not one, but two, security startups out of Israel for around $1 billion altogether to expand its portfolio of services.

> > Fact From Story Palo Alto Networks’ stock price has been on the rise on the back of strong earnings and growing demand for cybersecurity services, and now the company is using that momentum to do a little shopping.

> > > Fact From Story Specifically, it is looking at Talon Cyber Security — which has developed an enterprise browser aimed at security distributed workforces — for between $600 million and $700 million; and Dig Security — a specialist in securing data across public clouds — for between $300 million and $400 million.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge Acquiring companies with specialized services expands a company's portfolio.
> > Commonsense Knowledge A company's stock price rising indicates financial strength and the ability to make acquisitions.
> Commonsense Knowledge When a company negotiates to buy a startup, it is acquiring the startup.
